name: ColorModePicker
summary: Choose Light, Dark, or System as the color mode, with persistence.

useWhen: Letting people choose a light or dark presentation, or to follow their operating system's preference.
avoidWhen: When the application offers only a light and a dark choice and never follows the system; use ColorModeToggle.
When the product supports one fixed color scheme.

obligations: Exposes one radio group named Color mode, or by aria-label or aria-labelledby, whose radios are Light, Dark, and System.
Reads bounded localStorage and prefers-color-scheme without accessing browser globals during SSR.
Writes the Mux data-muxui-color-scheme hook on the document root.

behavior: The picker is a ToggleButtonGroup of three text options, Light, Dark, and System, with one selected and none able to be cleared.
The first render uses defaultMode, or System when it is not set, so server rendering and the first client render match.
localStorage and the operating system preference are read only after mount, never during server rendering.
After mount, the mode saved in localStorage under storageKey is restored when it is light or dark; any other saved value is ignored. Without one, defaultMode is used, and without that, System.
Light and Dark are written to data-muxui-color-scheme on the document root and saved under storageKey as light or dark, the format ColorModeToggle uses, so the two share a saved choice.

System removes the saved value from storage and writes the operating system's prefers-color-scheme to data-muxui-color-scheme, then follows later changes of that preference while System stays chosen. Choosing Light or Dark, or unmounting the picker, stops following and leaves the attribute as it was.
A change calls onModeChange with light, dark, or system; restoring a saved mode does not call it.
mode sets the selected option when the page controls it and is still written to the document root and storage; the picker does not change it, so the application updates mode.
The picker does not listen for changes to localStorage.
Nothing is written until the saved mode has been read, so a saved choice is never replaced by the default.
The picker is one radio group with one tab stop. Arrow keys move focus between the options, and Space or Enter selects the focused one.
The default name is Color mode. aria-label or aria-labelledby replaces it.
